entry.title: Monadically Dependent Graph Classes Have Almost Bounded Merge-Width
entry.summary:
A graph class $\mathcal{C}$ is monadically dependent if one cannot interpret all graphs in vertex-colored graphs from $\mathcal{C}$ using a fixed formula of first-order logic. We prove that every monadically dependent graph class has almost bounded merge-width, thereby confirming a conjecture of the first and the last author [STOC '25]. Our proof is algorithmic and the witnessing decompositions in the form of merge sequences can be computed in nearly-cubic time.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #algorithms #logic

entry.title: Finding full immersions is fixed-parameter tractable in labeled tour graphs
entry.summary:
We give an $O_H(n^5)$-time algorithm to test whether an $n$-vertex labeled tour graph has a full immersion isomorphic to a labeled tour graph $H$. A labeled tour graph is a connected $4$-regular graph whose edges are labeled by binary vectors of fixed length. To obtain a full immersion, a vertex may be removed only by pairing up its four incident edges and "splitting off" both pairs, summing the labels within each pair.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #algorithms #combinatorics

entry.title: A Quantum Lower Bound for Triangle Finding
entry.summary:
Triangle finding is a fundamental problem in graph theory that has played a central role in the development of quantum algorithmic techniques. For $N$-vertex graphs given by their adjacency matrices, a long line of work has improved the quantum query upper bound from $O(N^{3/2})$ to $O(N^{5/4})$. However, the best known lower bound has remained the elementary $Ω(N)$ bound obtained from unstructured search.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #quantum-computing #algorithms

entry.title: gcat, its_a_scam: modular tools for single cell data processing and per-cellquality control
entry.summary:
Motivation: The era of designing bioinformatic pipelines using open source tools is giving way to monolithic, and often proprietary, tools designed for end-to-end analysis, especially in the context of single cell data. While these tools are convenient for going from sequencing data to an almost complete data analysis "in a few clicks", they can strongly limit data use beyond standard analyses Results: We developed Gene and Chromosome Analysis Toolkit (gcat) and It's a scam To Sell Another Single Cell Analysis Method (its_a_scam) for modular processing and quality control of single cell genomic data, freeing users from their reliance on proprietary tools. gcat is a C++ library for parsing genomic data and working with it over genomic coordinates.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #distributed-systems

entry.title: Aggregate-Surplus Maximizing Monetary Policy -- by David Baqaee, Ariel Burstein, Joao Guerreiro
entry.summary:
We study optimal monetary policy in a general heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian (HANK) economy. Instead of maximizing a social welfare function, the policymaker maximizes the joint surplus of all households, without taking a stance on how that surplus should be distributed. This is the policy that maximizes resources left over if winners from reform were to compensate losers.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics #distributed-systems #agents

entry.title: Informing research priorities for distributed acoustic sensing: insights from a citizens' panel
entry.summary:
This report presents findings from a Citizens' Panel convened by the SOUNDSCALE project (www.soundscale.ac.uk) to inform research priorities for distributed acoustic sensing (DAS). Across three online and in-person workshops, 48 residents from Hampshire and London explored the technology's potential uses, risks, governance, and societal implications. The report summarises their deliberations and priorities, and reflects on the challenges of involving citizens in early-stage research on an unfamiliar technology.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #distributed-systems
